newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSI W Australia DRI plant said forging ahead.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSI W Australia DRI plant said forging ahead.

text.p: AUSI Ltd said its iron ore processing project in Western Australia's (WA) Pilbara region was forging ahead and that a new partner had been brought in.
Good progress was being made to take the AUSI direct reduced iron (DRI) project to financial close, chairman Sir Russel Madigan said in a statement.

Norwegian construction contractor Kvaerner ASA had signed as a primary shareholder in AUSI, joining other existing shareholders including Mobil Corp subsidiary Ampolex Ltd and German steelmaker Georgsmarienhutte, he said.

Senior Kvaerner executives Charles Boyle and John Fletcher had been appointed to the AUSI board and it was expected that Kvaerner/Davy, a Kvaerner group company, would undertake the turnkey design and construction contract for the AUSI DRI plant and associated infrastructure construction work, Madigan said.
"AUSI is poised to become WA's next processor and exporter of iron ore product," Madigan said.
Approval had been given to build the 3.6 million tonnes a year plant for the export of DRI to Asian markets, including China, South Korea and Indonesia, he said.
The plant would be located near Mt Anketal, 15 km west of Cape Lambert. Ship loading facilities and access corridors to iron ore and gas had also been defined, he said.
All necessary environment approvals were in hand and AUSI was "a long way down the track" with native title and heritage arrangements, he said.
Significant offtake letters of intent had been secured from major steel producers in the Asian region, he said.
These substantial developments signalled a dramatic move forward for the AUSI project, he said.
"No one else is better placed to establish Australia's next downstream iron processing facilities," he said.
The expertise and industry know-how of AUSI's three founding directors added weight to the consortium's front-runner position, he said.

Madigan was widely regarded as the prime mover in the development of the WA iron ore induistry, Sir Roderick Carnegie was a leading figure in the deregulation of gas in WA while economist Ross Garnaut was a former Australian Ambassador to the People's Republic of China, the statement said.
China was likely to take a large slice of AUSI product, Madigan said.

AUSI expects to complete its project financing stage in the second quarter of 1997 when construction of the Mt Anketal plant was expected to begin, with production starting in the third quarter of 1999, Madigan said.
The project will employ 2,000 people at peak level during construction and will have an operating workforce of about 350.
AUSI's DRI processing plant will be the biggest in the world at 3.6 million tonne capacity, the statement added.
